implementationNotes: GameAction.TransferPreparedCard carries prepared deck UUID, concrete card UUID, decimal identity index and captured source section, with game/preparation scope and no invitation/play scope. Server derives actor/destination, validates the seed/index/section and executes the same PreparationRules.transfer used for provisional display. Splitting and canonical contiguous recompaction retain every UUID/definition/selected metadata without per-quantity allocation; persisted V8 encoding is unchanged and actual stored copies reopen across runtime restart.

Each card has an individual original request/result and accepted revision/outbox transaction. Captured all never consults a later row quantity or mutable saved source. A conflicting constituent rejects without substitution or cancelling independent valid work. Same-ID retries return original outcomes; changed intent is refused. Wrong prepared deck/card/section/round/lobby/account refuses with no accepted-state mutation. Existing privacy, source deletion isolation and same-round invitation replacements remain intact; no new bulk mutation, processor, whole-lobby lock or format/size/exchange rule.

Production controller captures personal immutable row ranges at gesture start and releases through the session. Selection and invitation controls retain their existing gate, but transfers pipeline independently, including behind an unacknowledged selection. Accepted state remains revisioned; receipts/results never become old-state snapshots. Surviving original predictions rebase after accepted changes, correlated revisions or commit-revision results retire only their predictions, inapplicable prediction can withdraw without recalling the original, and late acceptance is ordinary accepted state.

The existing recovery protocol accepts at most 256 original IDs. Session active originals remain inside that window; a larger invocation retains all remaining captured ranges compactly and exposes queuedTransferCards. Full intended display is immediate, the tail drains in captured order as capacity returns, and a 300-card drain plus Int.MAX_VALUE compact capture test prove no truncation or huge per-card allocation. Same-process reconnect/reauthentication retains originals and tail; Logout/account switch clears/fences, and a fresh process synchronizes accepted state without outgoing persistence.

The initial affected command passed shared/client, actual pipelined socket and partial-outcome database assertions, then failed only the injected-SQL rollback harness at a premature service head read (NOT_OWNER). Production ownership invalidation is correct. The test now checks persisted preparation/revision directly while unavailable and then proves ordinary runtime restart/stream recovery; only that failed server test was rerun. Final controller state adds the queued-card count, plus pending-selection and account-switch regression checks; its affected tests/APK compile run passes. Initial failure remains diagnostic, not relabeled green. No broad/fault/device recertification.
